headline: Sell Atlanta first, the Hawks second: city codes, a co-created MLK night and paid local tastemakers.

archetype.name: The Culture Capital's Swing Fans
archetype.description: A Black-led, metro-wide crowd that treats the arena as a runway and Atlanta itself as the team; loyal in spirit, loud only when the night means something (MLK Day, a big home Cup night, a playoff series).

pulse.teamMoment: Jalen Johnson's Hawks (46-36, No. 6 seed, lost 4-2 to the champion Knicks after leading 2-1) reloaded around defense under Quin Snyder with No. 8 pick Kingston Flemings, Lu Dort, Ryan Nembhard, Aaron Wiggins and Devin Carter, while 2024 No. 1 pick Zaccharie Risacher went to Dallas.
pulse.sentiment: Cautiously optimistic: an All-NBA Johnson, a Most Improved Alexander-Walker and a deep defense give hope, but the 2-1 collapse to New York and the end of the Trae Young chapter keep fans guarded and waiting for proof.

verifiedMoment: Jalen Johnson's Hawks reloaded around defense after a 6-seed season: No. 8 pick Kingston Flemings, plus trades for Lu Dort, Ryan Nembhard, Aaron Wiggins and Devin Carter, with 2024 No. 1 pick Zaccharie Risacher shipped to Dallas.

scorecard.rationale: Atlanta has one of the league's deepest design wells (Black Mecca, hip-hop, HBCU, rink and car culture, an immigrant 770) and a big, style-literate metro, but Hawks fandom runs below the city's cultural heat and arrives in spikes. Retail is broad yet car-dependent and split by trade area, with taste set in small independent doors whose status needs checking.

headline: Boston backs the banners while it doubts the roster: sell heritage, winter and neighborhoods, not players.

archetype.name: The Banner Counters
archetype.description: A multigenerational fan base that measures itself in titles and treats Celtics history as family property. Loyalty attaches to the green, the banners and the parquet first and to players a distant second, which is exactly what a reset season needs.

pulse.teamMoment: The Tatum-Brown era is over: after a 56-26 season ended in a 3-1 first-round collapse to Philadelphia, Brad Stevens traded Jaylen Brown to the 76ers for Paul George and picks and rebuilt around Jayson Tatum with Mitchell Robinson, Mike Conley and an extended Neemias Queta.
pulse.sentiment: Unsettled and skeptical: proud of Banner 18, bruised by the collapse, split on the Brown trade, and wary of George's age and contract after Tatum's father publicly criticized the roster and national free-agency grades panned the summer.

verifiedMoment: The Tatum-Brown era is over: after a 3-1 first-round collapse against Philadelphia, Brad Stevens traded Jaylen Brown to the 76ers for Paul George and picks and rebuilt the roster around Jayson Tatum.

scorecard.rationale: Boston pairs one of the league's most intense, heritage-driven fan bases and a deep, distinct civic and neighborhood culture with strong retail (the Garden, Newbury, Concepts, regional outlets), but the opportunity is capped this season by roster doubt and by rival brands' home-turf claims.

A UV-reactive interior reveals the retired-number row, which fans decode online; keep the parquet tonal and anchor every graphic to a named Garden reference.

headline: Sell Brooklyn the city, not New York's other team: 112 codes, civic gilt and drops co-authored block by block.

archetype.name: The Borough Separatists
archetype.description: An outnumbered, style-literate tribe that treats the Nets as proof Brooklyn is its own city. Loyalty is to the borough first and the roster third, so it survives losing but punishes anything that reads as Manhattan, tourist or transplant.

pulse.teamMoment: A development year after a 20-62 season: No. 6 pick Mikel Brown Jr. and Egor Demin lead a very young roster beside veteran scorers Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr. and new guard Keon Ellis, under newly extended Jordi Fernandez, with no opening-night or Christmas Day game.
pulse.sentiment: Patient, wry and mildly hopeful about the kids, and defiant about being Brooklyn while the defending-champion Knicks own the city's attention.

verifiedMoment: The Nets are still rebuilding, but with more veteran scoring: Julius Randle returns to New York alongside Michael Porter Jr., and No. 6 pick Mikel Brown Jr. leads a very young roster under a newly extended Jordi Fernandez.

scorecard.rationale: Brooklyn's culture is among the deepest and most designable in the league, but the Nets' fandom is thin after 20-62 in a Knicks title year and most partners and doors are unchecked. The opportunity rests on the borough mark selling without wins, and is conditional on local co-authorship and a 2027 build rather than this season.

opportunities.summary: This season's only real product lane: screen-printed tees, crewnecks and print-on-demand 112 ZIP numerals in black and bone, speaking as the City of Brooklyn, launched around the Nov. 3 anniversary and the start of the 15th Brooklyn season.

opportunities.how: Run on existing licensed blanks through the NBA licensing channel; on-site ZIP printing only if BSE Global and the Nets Shop operator agree. Hangtags tell the civic story through lettering, never Dodgers marks.

scorecard.rationale: Chicago is one of the league's deepest design cultures and a global heritage retail engine with a full flagship, arena, boutique and suburban-mall network. archetype.description: A fan base that carried The Drive, The Fumble and The Shot for 52 years until the 2016 comeback from 3-1 down, and that met last spring's 125-94 Game 7 rout of Detroit with a shrug until the Knicks series was won. It trusts only what is earned, rewards local craft, and punishes hype or outsider jokes about the city.

pulse.teamMoment: Coming off 52-30, two Game 7 wins (including a 125-94 rout of No. 1 Detroit) and an East Finals sweep by the eventual champion Knicks, Cleveland went all in: Mitchell extended, Harden re-signed and the last tradable first spent on Peyton Watson. It is a title-or-bust season with no opening-night or Christmas Day game.
pulse.sentiment: Optimistic and impatient: fans believe after the playoff run but the Knicks sweep, thinner depth (Wade, Ellis and Nance gone) and a scout's public doubt keep them guarded about championship talk.

verifiedMoment: Cleveland is all in. The Cavs reached their first conference finals since 2018, then re-signed James Harden, extended Donovan Mitchell and spent their last tradable first on Peyton Watson. It is a title-or-bust season.

scorecard.rationale: Cleveland has unusually deep, designable local culture (punk and rap lineage, ore-dock steel and Deco civic stone, immigrant food rituals, a distinct Akron identity) and a loyal, title-hungry regional fan base, but a drive-to-the-mall retail map with no downtown sneaker district, a Browns-first fall wallet and a LeBron storyline Nike must handle carefully cap the near-term upside.

headline: Detroit wears the city before the team: co-author with its makers, build it to be worn in, talk like a shift.

archetype.name: The Blue-Collar Contender
archetype.description: A fan base that defines itself by effort, defense and being counted out, now holding a 60-win team it does not yet fully trust. It rewards grit and local credit and punishes gloss, hype and outsider 'comeback city' pity.

pulse.teamMoment: After 60-22, the East's No. 1 seed and a 4-3 second-round loss to Cleveland capped by a 125-94 Game 7, Detroit kept its core (Jalen Duren re-signed for 5 years and $200M, Isaiah Stewart traded to Memphis) and added John Collins, Isaiah Joe, Taurean Prince, Gary Harris and rookie Ebuka Okorie under J.B. Bickerstaff. It opens Oct 20 hosting Boston on NBC and has no Christmas Day game.
pulse.sentiment: Proud but nervous: Cade Cunningham's All-NBA First Team year and Duren's deal feel earned, but the Game 7 blowout is raw and fans and analysts doubt there is a second creator beside Cade.

verifiedMoment: After a 60-win, No. 1-seed season ended in a Game 7 blowout loss to Cleveland, Detroit kept its core: Jalen Duren signed for $200M. The open question is whether Cade Cunningham has enough help without a second star.

scorecard.rationale: A 60-win No. 1 seed in a Specter year, three heritage wardrobes and a seven-month outerwear season put opportunity well above average, and in our judgment Detroit's design well (Motown, techno, jit, Dilla, Pewabic, Deco, workwear, immigrant corridors) is unusually deep. Retail is scored cautiously because the city core is thin and key partner doors (Detroit vs. Everybody, Two18, Nike Factory at Great Lakes Crossing) are unconfirmed; fandom is intense but shares winter with the Lions and Red Wings and is anxious after the Game 7 rout.

headline: Indiana is where the game lives: Hinkle week, 92 county numbers and the Avenue, worn in Pacers navy and gold.

archetype.name: The Keepers of the Gym
archetype.description: Fans raised on a single-class state tournament that ran until 1997, county gyms that out-seat their towns, and Hinkle's 1928 barrel vault. They reward effort over flash and wear navy and gold as Pacers loyalty that travels from Mass Ave to New Castle.

pulse.teamMoment: Tyrese Haliburton is back from the Achilles tear he suffered in Game 7 of the 2025 Finals and rejoins Siakam, Nembhard, Nesmith, McConnell and deadline pickup Ivica Zubac under Rick Carlisle after a 19-63 season, with Kelly Oubre Jr., Larry Nance Jr. and two-way Purdue guard Braden Smith added. Indiana hosts the 76ers on the Oct 30 opening Cup Night and has no opening-night or Christmas Day game.
pulse.sentiment: Cautiously hopeful and protective: fans expect a bounce-back toward contention but remember how fast the 2025 high ended, and they will punish anything that feels like hype or exploits the injury.

verifiedMoment: Tyrese Haliburton is back from the torn Achilles he suffered in Game 7 of the 2025 Finals ('I am healthy, ready to go,' Sept 28). He rejoins the Siakam-led 2025 Finals core, now with Ivica Zubac at center, after a lost 19-63 year.

scorecard.rationale: Indiana has one of the league's deepest basketball cultures and a one-off Hinkle Cup final in a comeback season, which lifts opportunity above average despite a small market. Retail sits below average: no destination flagship, a mall-first, value-led buyer, a star with a rival footwear deal and key cues that need third-party clearance.

headline: Giannis joins Heat Culture: win Miami court by court and barrio by barrio, in three languages, built for heat.

archetype.description: A multinational, trilingual crowd that judges the Heat on effort and playoff nights, dresses for the arena like it is dinner or the club, and now expects a championship from a Giannis-Bam contender.

pulse.teamMoment: After a 43-39, No. 10-seed season that ended in a 127-126 overtime Play-In loss at Charlotte, Miami traded Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel'el Ware and a haul of picks for Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis, then signed Klay Thompson. Under Erik Spoelstra, a Giannis-Bam Adebayo frontcourt makes 2026-27 title-or-bust.
pulse.sentiment: Euphoric and demanding: the mood flipped from Play-In frustration to championship expectation, with real worry about depth after losing Herro, Jaquez, Ware and Norman Powell, and ESPN openly doubting the supporting cast.

verifiedMoment: Miami landed Giannis Antetokounmpo in one of the biggest trades in NBA history and added Klay Thompson. It is now a Giannis-Bam Adebayo contender on paper, and anything short of a deep run will read as failure.

scorecard.rationale: A Nike signature superstar arriving in a gateway shopping market, with some of the league's deepest multicultural design material and a real park-court culture, puts opportunity and culture near the top of the league. Retail is strong but sprawling and knockoff-pressured, and fandom peaks on White Hot playoff nights but is more front-running than the league's most loyal markets.

headline: With Giannis gone, the Bucks belong to Cream City again: sell the brick, the cold and the neighborhoods, not a new star.

archetype.name: The Working-City Loyalist
archetype.description: A statewide, blue-collar fan base that expects to be overlooked, values effort over glamour and stays loyal through a rebuild, but punishes anything that talks down to it or cashes in on its grief.

pulse.teamMoment: Milwaukee opens 2026-27 rebuilding after trading Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis to Miami, with new coach Taylor Jenkins and a core of Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel'el Ware, Myles Turner, Kyle Kuzma and rookie Brayden Burries, coming off a 32-50 season.
pulse.sentiment: Grief and some anger over the trade, resignation about a long rebuild, and cautious curiosity about Herro and the rookies; nostalgia for 2021 is the safest emotion, and Jan 28 is circled by everyone.

verifiedMoment: Milwaukee faces its first season without Giannis Antetokounmpo in more than a decade, with a new coach in Taylor Jenkins. The Bucks are starting a long rebuild around Tyler Herro, the young pieces from the Miami trade and two lottery picks.

scorecard.rationale: Milwaukee has one of the league's most place-specific palettes and a deep tavern and neighborhood vernacular, but a small, value-minded market in a low-expectation rebuild, a thin sneaker scene and no Nike-owned door in the city keep opportunity average and retail below average, which is why the plan runs only three priority-1 bets. Fandom is loyal and statewide but at low heat until Jan 28.

headline: 53 years, then a ring: sell New York's title through its parks, counters and borough doors, not its skyline.

archetype.name: The Vindicated Lifers
archetype.description: A multigenerational, five-borough fan base that kept selling out the Mecca through 53 ringless years and now wants to say 'told you' in its own codes. It values grit, defense and heritage over flash and spots anything corporate or touristy from a block away.

pulse.teamMoment: Defending champions after a 53-29 season and a 16-3 playoff run capped by Brunson's Finals MVP and a 94-90 Game 5 clincher over San Antonio; the core is intact under the second apron, and the defense opens with ring night against LeBron James' and Jaylen Brown's 76ers on Oct 20.
pulse.sentiment: Euphoric and protective: fans are flush with the first title since 1973 and expect a real defense in a tougher East, with old ownership grievances quieter but not forgotten.

verifiedMoment: The defending champions: the Knicks won their first title since 1973, with Jalen Brunson as Finals MVP. They kept most of the roster under the second apron, and the defense starts with a ring night against LeBron James and Jaylen Brown's new-look 76ers.

scorecard.rationale: The league's biggest market defending its first title in 53 years, with the deepest homegrown basketball, music and art culture to design from. Scores are held down because it is also the most crowded, license-heavy market (MSG, MTA, Puma's Clyde, Fanatics, a locked 2026-27 City Edition), so Nike's real lanes are the AF1 Uptowns and Flax, Specter, the park circuit and the borough doors, all assuming rights and doors check out.

They are loyal to 'our guys', nostalgic for Penny's pinstripes, and allergic to being mistaken for tourists, especially when visiting fans fill Kia Center.

pulse.teamMoment: Orlando chose continuity: Jamahl Mosley was fired after a 45-37 season that ended with a Play-In escape and a first-round loss to No. 1 Detroit, Sean Sweeney arrived from San Antonio, and Vucevic is back beside Banchero, Wagner and Bane. The open questions are Wagner's health after 34 games and three ball-dominant stars with no true point guard.
pulse.sentiment: Cautiously hopeful but impatient: fans like the core and Vucevic's return, but the mood has moved from 'rebuild' to 'prove it', and nobody wants hype before results.

verifiedMoment: Orlando chose continuity over a splash: it fired Jamahl Mosley, hired Spurs defensive architect Sean Sweeney and is betting he can make the Banchero-Wagner-Bane trio work. Vucevic is back for his second Magic stint.

scorecard.rationale: Opportunity sits above average because Nike owns the Penny-pinstripe nostalgia and Central Florida's Puerto Rican and tourist audiences are large, but no national-TV stage, modest local incomes and a prove-it season cap it. Culture is deep (Parramore, OBT signage, Mills 50, Boricua Orlando), though the score assumes partners the brief has not yet signed; retail is outlet-heavy with a thin taste layer, and fandom is loyal but playoff-gated.

headline: Philly loves a Sixer who earns it: build from the gym, the order counter and Broad Street, not from 1776.

pulse.teamMoment: After a 45-37 Play-In season, a comeback from 3-1 down against No. 2 Boston and a second-round sweep by the eventual champion Knicks, Philly traded Paul George for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join Embiid, Maxey and Edgecombe. Title odds moved to about +1000, and Nick Nurse is under maximum pressure.
pulse.sentiment: Giddy but braced. The city knows Embiid's availability, LeBron turning 42 in December and the fresh Knicks wound decide the year, and it will judge both new stars on effort, not reputation.

verifiedMoment: Philadelphia had the summer's biggest swing: Jaylen Brown arrived by trade from Boston and LeBron James signed as a free agent, joining Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe. The questions are health and age, and Nick Nurse is under maximum pressure.

scorecard.rationale: A title-contending superteam with Nike's LeBron, a Specter season and a new arena coming to the Spectrum site make this one of the league's biggest 2026-27 openings, and few markets offer as deep a culture to design from. Retail is broad but the taste-setting independents are thin since Ubiq closed and the throwback lane belongs to Mitchell & Ness, and fan intensity is elite but shares the winter with the Eagles.

archetype.description: A Black-built, DMV-wide fan base that has stayed loyal to the District and the 1978 banner more than to the modern Wizards, and wears DC civic symbols as identity. It commits to the team when the team speaks DC and shows up East of the River, not on the Mall.

pulse.teamMoment: Washington went from the NBA's worst record (17-65) to winning the lottery: No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa joins Trae Young (re-signed for about $212M over four years), Anthony Davis and young core Alex Sarr, Kyshawn George and Tre Johnson under Brian Keefe. There is no opening-night or Christmas game; the first confirmed home date of note is the Oct 30 Cup Night against Charlotte in East Group C, a regional rather than national stage.
pulse.sentiment: Cautiously curious: real excitement about Dybantsa and the Young-Davis pairing, wrapped in gallows humor and a show-me demand for proof on health and fit before fans fully commit.

verifiedMoment: Washington jumped from the NBA's worst record to a fascinating build: lottery winner AJ Dybantsa joins Trae Young (re-signed long term), Anthony Davis and young core pieces Alex Sarr, Kyshawn George and Tre Johnson.

scorecard.rationale: DC has one of the league's deepest and most ownable local cultures (an official music, a beloved civic flag and type system, Chocolate City and DMV hoops), and the Dybantsa reset makes this an above-average opening. Fandom sits below average after 17-65 in a hockey-first, visiting-fan-heavy arena, and retail is a wealthy but fragmented suburban mall-and-DTLR market, so the plan is held to three priorities with gates.

pulse.teamMoment: After a 54-28 season ended in a 4-2 first-round upset by sixth-seeded Minnesota, Denver is betting on continuity around three-time MVP Nikola Jokic under coach David Adelman, adding 37-year-old DeMar DeRozan on a one-year deal and sitting at a 49.5 win total, a second-tier contender behind OKC and San Antonio.

verifiedMoment: Denver is betting on continuity around three-time MVP Nikola Jokic after a first-round upset. It added DeMar DeRozan for scoring, and Jokic is eligible for a roughly $290M extension he has said he aims to sign.

scorecard.rationale: A three-time MVP, a recent title, one of the league's most loved vintage graphics and a long outerwear season make Denver an above-average opportunity with deep design material. Retail is below average (no downtown Nike door, thin sneaker-boutique scene, volume on the suburban edges), and fandom is loyal but quiet until the playoffs.

headline: Oakland is the soul, San Francisco the address: win the Bay on the bridge between them, in gear built for fog.

archetype.name: The Dynasty Diaspora
archetype.description: A fan base forged in 40 lean Oakland years and spoiled by four titles, now spread across The Town, The City and the 408. It is loyal to Curry, Draymond and Kerr more than to an arena, and it is nostalgic for Oracle in a building that never had Oracle's soul.

pulse.teamMoment: Curry's aging core ran it back after a 37-45 season, a play-in win over the Clippers and a 111-96 loss at Phoenix: the Warriors chased Giannis and Anthony Davis without a deal, re-signed Porzingis, Horford, Melton and Gary Payton II, added Niang and Brandon Williams, drafted Yaxel Lendeborg at No. 11, and have Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody recovering from injury.
pulse.sentiment: Grateful and anxious: fans are invested in the dynasty-era window but expect little (a 40.5 win total, with previews doubting a play-in spot), so the mood favors keepsake and heritage buying over hype.

verifiedMoment: Stephen Curry's aging core ran it back after failing to land another star (the Warriors explored Giannis and Anthony Davis). Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are still recovering from injuries.

scorecard.rationale: Culture is near the top (two cities, three subcultural lineages, huge Asian American communities), but opportunity is held to the low 70s by a 40.5 win total, injured Butler and Moody, an open Curry deal and a winter-only window. A Curry-Nike deal, confirmed Specter game dates and a hot November would move it back toward 80.

headline: Sell Houston's finish, not its logo: candy paint, Clutch City red and gold, and a hoops lineage nobody else can claim.

archetype.name: The Overlooked Originators
archetype.description: A hyper-diverse, Black-and-brown metro that invented slab, screw and Clutch City and still feels underrated next to Dallas and the coasts. They reward brands that credit the source and punish ones that borrow the look.

pulse.teamMoment: After a 52-30 season and a 4-2 first-round loss to the Lakers, Houston kept Ime Udoka and the Durant-Sengun core, extended Amen Thompson (5 years, $208M) and Tari Eason (5 years, $81.5M), and added Marcus Smart, Bogdan Bogdanovic and shooting coach Chip Engelland; BetMGM sets the win total at 47.5.
pulse.sentiment: Judgment call, not measured: hopeful but impatient after a first-round exit, with a 47.5 win total and summer Durant trade chatter keeping expectations flatter than last year's 52 wins.

verifiedMoment: Houston kept Ime Udoka and the Kevin Durant-Alperen Sengun core, locked up Amen Thompson and Tari Eason, and added veterans Marcus Smart and Bogdan Bogdanovic after a first-round exit.

scorecard.rationale: Houston has one of the league's deepest and most specific design wells (slab, grillz, Black cowboy style, a full basketball lineage and the country's most diverse neighborhoods) and a 52-win team with Durant and a newly extended young core. Retail is big but car-dependent and spread thin, the 47.5 win total signals a flatter outlook, and the Rockets fight football, the Astros and the rodeo for attention.

archetype.description: A polite but stubborn statewide fan base that wears its scars (Garnett's exit, the drought, a former Wolf winning a title in New York) and wants belief, not victory laps. It dresses for wind chill below zero and reps area codes and neighborhoods before skylines.

pulse.teamMoment: New coach Jamahl Mosley inherits Zion Williamson, breakout scorer Trey Murphy III (21.5 ppg, kept through June trade rumors) and second-year Derik Queen and Jeremiah Fears after a 26-56 season and a quiet offseason under Joe Dumars. The team is not on the opening-night or Christmas slates; NBA Cup West Group B (OKC, MIN, LAC, MEM), opening Oct 30 at the Clippers, is the early-season stage.

archetype.name: The One-Team State
archetype.description: A whole state that adopted a franchise in 2008 and now wears a champion as its civic uniform. Loud, loyal, value-minded and allergic to flash the team has not earned.

pulse.teamMoment: Back-to-back MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's Thunder went 64-18 and are 2026-27 co-title favorites (BetMGM win total 60.5, the West's highest) after San Antonio beat them 4-3 in the West finals. headline: Own the '77-at-50 heritage gap in Nike's hometown: built for the Big Dark, co-authored with Albina.

archetype.name: The Insider Loyalist
archetype.description: A fan base that stayed through 814 sellouts, the Jail Blazers and Lillard's exit and return, and that reads every jersey for fabric, fit and who designed it because it lives next door to Beaverton. It wants its own story told from inside the city, never a Portlandia punchline.

pulse.teamMoment: New owner Tom Dundon's Blazers add Ja Morant (acquired from Memphis on June 29) to a backcourt with Damian Lillard, back from a torn Achilles, under first-year coach Micah Nori, after a 42-40 season that ended 4-1 to San Antonio in the first round. Oregon, Multnomah County and Portland have committed $586M toward Moda Center upgrades, but the lease is still unsigned.
pulse.sentiment: Hopeful but guarded: emotional about Lillard back in a Blazers uniform after a lost season, split on Morant's talent versus his 2023 suspensions, debating whether Nori brings one of them off the bench, and relieved the team is staying while wary of an owner who says he won't pay for the renovation.

verifiedMoment: New owner Tom Dundon's Blazers add Ja Morant to a backcourt with Damian Lillard, back from a torn Achilles, under first-year coach Micah Nori. The Moda Center renovation lease is still being negotiated.

scorecard.rationale: A once-only heritage year, an empty City Edition slot and a deep roster in Nike's own hometown make the opportunity large, and Albina, Rip City broadcast lore, maker craft and supporter culture give unusually deep design material. Retail lags because the metro has few public Nike doors, a thinned downtown and a Rose Quarter retail desert, and this season's lead times limit what can ship before February; fandom is intense and statewide but guarded about Morant and the owner.

headline: Sell Sacramento the team it kept: purple for the Kings, bridge bronze for the city, the Beam as its signature.

archetype.name: The Keepers
archetype.description: A fan base that personally rescued its team and now treats every home game as civic duty. It forgives losing but not condescension, and it punishes anything that reads as Bay Area, Lakers or outsider.

pulse.teamMoment: A youth movement after a 22-60 season and a lost lottery tiebreak: No. 7 pick Darius Acuff Jr. joins Domantas Sabonis, Zach LaVine and Malik Monk under Doug Christie in his second full season, with no opening-night or Christmas Day game and a Cup group with the Spurs, Lakers, Warriors and Trail Blazers.
pulse.sentiment: Patient, defiant and a little sour. Fans are tired of losing and wary of the roster, but they quote the 'going to be bad' forecasts back with a chip on their shoulder and are ready to back Acuff, Sabonis and Christie.

verifiedMoment: A youth movement led by No. 7 pick Darius Acuff Jr. around holdovers Domantas Sabonis, Zach LaVine and Malik Monk. Sacramento is widely projected near the bottom of the West.

scorecard.rationale: Loyalty is well above league average because fans saved the team, and the bridge, the Beam and the neighborhood scenes give real design material. headline: Silver and black every day, Fiesta color for the occasion: win San Antonio through its makers, its April and its whole map.

archetype.description: A multigenerational, Latino-majority, military-heavy fan base that spans the West, East and South Sides, treats the Spurs as the city's shared family table, prizes humility over flash, and now expects a title after losing the 2026 Finals.

pulse.teamMoment: The 2026 West champions (62-20, beat OKC 4-3 in the West finals) lost the Finals 4-1 to the Knicks, then extended Wembanyama (5 years, $252M) and Fox (through 2029-30) and run the core back under Mitch Johnson as title co-favorites with OKC. scorecard.rationale: A title co-favorite led by Wembanyama, in a one-team region that runs to Mexico, with some of the league's most specific design material (Fiesta, conjunto, West Side craft, the East Side's Iceman lineage), puts opportunity, culture and fandom well above average. pulse.sentiment: Impatient but curious: tired after a bottom-of-the-league year, energized by Peterson and the Jackson Jr. trade, and expecting visible progress and a play-in chase rather than a playoff run.

verifiedMoment: Utah's youth movement speeds up with No. 2 pick Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey alongside veterans Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr., and Will Hardy is under pressure to develop them.

scorecard.rationale: A small metro but a whole-state, family-sized, youth-heavy buyer base with deep one-team loyalty and an unusually distinct design vocabulary (salt, snow, all-ages DIY, West Side hoops). Retail is dispersed along I-15 with a thin boutique layer, and a rebuild year with no national stage caps the near-term upside.

opportunities.title: Peterson-Bailey Family Pack
opportunities.summary: A youth-first player program built for multi-kid households: Peterson and Bailey youth jerseys and tees, toddler sizes, and matching kid-to-adult sets ready before the first home Cup Night.
where: Jazz and Nike e-commerce for out-of-metro fans
opportunities.when: Mid-October launch through Christmas Eve, peaking at the first home game and Black Friday
opportunities.how: Stock deeper on Peterson and Bailey than legacy names, with Markkanen and Jackson Jr. as the adult core, all in the current purple Icon and black Statement looks. Sell bundle pricing and coordinated family sets with a Jazz Bear kids' hook, and launch in-store on a Saturday, never a Sunday.
opportunities.segment: Families and youth across the Wasatch Front
products: Markkanen and Jackson Jr. adult player hoodies

opportunities.title: Inversion Layer Cold-Weather Line
opportunities.summary: The repeat City Edition reframed as Utah material: a Nike-only gray-to-baby-blue outerwear and fleece line with salt-crackle and granite-speckle textures, built for the canyon commute and the walk into the Delta Center.
opportunities.when: Launch with ski-resort openings in mid-to-late November and sell through spring skiing
opportunities.how: Tell the inversion-haze-to-clear-sky story on hangtags and in-store, build within ACG and NBA outerwear using local technical codes (shell cut, snap pockets, drawcords) with no outside brand, and sell it as the Christmas gift for the fan who skis.
opportunities.segment: Statewide outdoor-oriented fans and families

opportunities.title: West Side Court Collective
opportunities.summary: A co-designed capsule with Tongan, Samoan and Latino designers from Rose Park, Glendale, West Valley and Kearns, sold at community events and named West Side doors and funding youth rec basketball.
where: Sorenson Unity Center and community courts in Glendale and Rose Park
Valley Fair Mall, West Valley City (confirm door)
opportunities.when: Commission in winter, reveal at Living Traditions in May, sell through the park-court season and Hispanic Heritage Month
opportunities.how: Recruit and pay designers through the Salt Lake Arts Council's artist networks and a Latino arts partner such as Mestizo Institute of Culture and Arts, with PIK2AR and Centro Civico Mexicano as cultural reviewers. Give Tongan, Samoan and Latino designers separate credit and approval, route a share of proceeds to West Side rec leagues, and launch court-side, not downtown.
opportunities.segment: Pacific Islander and Latino hoop families on the West Side

opportunities.title: Delta Night Poster Series
opportunities.summary: One screen-printed gig-poster tee per month of home games, made with local poster artists and printers in the Kilby Court and SLUG Magazine tradition, packaged like a 7-inch single.
opportunities.when: First drop at Kilby Court on Fri Oct 30 (the Nuggets Cup Night), then monthly through April
opportunities.how: Commission a different Utah artist each month through Craft Lake City and SLUG, print locally in limited runs with off-register ink in Jazz purple, black and sky blue plus newsprint cream, and release on Gallery Stroll Fridays. A sleeve-style hangtag carries a local-artist playlist QR.
opportunities.segment: Gen Z and Sugar House creative fans

opportunities.title: Note Era and Mountain Era Capsules
opportunities.summary: Separate heritage capsules for the 1979-96 Note, the 1996 Mountain look and the 2017-22 Mitchell-Gobert playoff years, with the New Orleans origin told on labels and inserts.
where: Delta Center team store on legend nights
opportunities.when: December gifting, with a second push around a midseason legend or throwback night
opportunities.how: Confirm which licensee holds Note and Mountain heritage jerseys before promising one; Nike leads tees, fleece and warm-ups under team and NBA licensing. Use the team mark for the New Orleans chapter, clear any player names through the NBPA or estates, and bridge to the rookies with a Peterson tee in an era palette.
opportunities.segment: Heritage diehards and parents buying for kids

opportunities.title: I-15 Saturday Pop-ups
opportunities.summary: Satellite Saturday pop-ups in Ogden and Provo-Orem so fans who reach the Delta Center only once a season can buy close to home, plus Salt Lake City Stars G League games as an entry-price door.
where: Salt Lake City Stars home games
opportunities.when: Saturdays from Nov 7 through the gifting season, never Halloween or a Sunday
opportunities.how: Rotate a mobile shop through the corridor stops on Saturdays only, starting Nov 7, with a Jazz Bear appearance for kids and a stop-exclusive colorway. Add a family-priced table at Stars games, and send Sunday and General Conference shoppers to e-commerce.
opportunities.segment: Statewide and rural fans and Utah County families

opportunities.title: Draft Night to Summer League
opportunities.summary: Owning the offseason that this prospect-obsessed fan base actually follows: a draft-night rookie tee, a Salt Lake City Summer League pop-up and park-court season product.
opportunities.when: Late June draft through mid-July Summer League
opportunities.how: Print the new pick's tee within hours of draft night, run one Summer League pop-up for the most engaged fans, and back it with lightweight park-court product for the hot, dry summer.
opportunities.segment: Diehards and Gen Z fans tracking prospects

calendar.window: Oct 12-29, after General Conference weekend
calendar.moment: Season launch ahead of the first home game
calendar.play: Land the Peterson-Bailey family program in the team store, Murray and Orem doors with a Saturday in-store launch, and anchor the arena moment to the first confirmed home date.

calendar.window: Fri Oct 30
calendar.moment: Nuggets at Jazz, opening NBA Cup Night
calendar.play: Drop poster tee No. 1 at Kilby Court and the team store; skip Halloween Saturday and open the first I-15 pop-up in Ogden on Sat Nov 7.

calendar.window: Mid-to-late November, with resort openings
calendar.moment: Wasatch ski season opens
calendar.play: Launch the Inversion Layer line in the team store, Murray, Orem and City Creek, merchandised with ACG.

calendar.window: Thanksgiving week and Black Friday
calendar.moment: Family gathering week and gifting kickoff
calendar.play: Run family bundles and kids' gradient hoodies through doors and e-commerce regardless of the schedule; add arena moments only on confirmed home Cup dates.

calendar.window: Dec 1-24
calendar.moment: Local family gifting peak (no Christmas Day game)
calendar.play: Release the heritage capsules as gifts in 7-inch sleeve boxes; push Sunday shoppers to e-commerce.

calendar.window: Third Friday (Gallery Stroll) and peak ski weeks
calendar.moment: Gallery Stroll and mid-winter
calendar.play: Poster tee release at a Gallery Stroll pop-up; begin paid commissioning for the West Side Court Collective.

calendar.window: Feb 11 trade deadline
calendar.moment: Deadline and roster reset
calendar.play: Re-weight player-graphic inventory toward whoever is carrying the team; keep fast-print capacity ready.

calendar.window: Late Feb to mid-March
calendar.moment: High school state tournaments and the play-in decision
calendar.play: Gift practice tees to West Side high school programs; green-light a play-in tee only if Utah sits 7-10 in mid-March.

calendar.window: Apr 11 season end, Apr 13-16 play-in
calendar.moment: Season close (avoid General Conference weekend)
calendar.play: Run the final poster tee and outerwear clearance online; no in-person events on Conference weekend.

calendar.window: Mid-to-late May
calendar.moment: Living Traditions Festival
calendar.play: Reveal the West Side Court Collective with its designers, alongside the Salt Lake Arts Council and the community partners.

calendar.window: Late June
calendar.moment: NBA Draft
calendar.play: Draft-night rookie tee within hours of the pick, sold online first.

calendar.window: Early-to-mid July
calendar.moment: Salt Lake City Summer League
calendar.play: One Summer League pop-up at the Delta Center. Pioneer Day (July 24) is a retail-traffic note only, with no themed product.

calendar.window: Mid-August
calendar.moment: Craft Lake City DIY Fest, Speed Week and back to school
calendar.play: Scout next season's poster artists at DIY Fest and run a kids' back-to-school jersey push.

calendar.window: Mid-September to mid-October
calendar.moment: Hispanic Heritage Month and training camp
calendar.play: Second West Side Court Collective drop led by its Latino designers, plus new-season jersey previews.
